summary_en: This phase 1 study tests BP1002, a liposomal Bcl-2 antisense oligodeoxynucleotide, in adults with refractory or relapsed acute myeloid leukemia (AML). BP1002 is first given alone at escalating doses and later with decitabine; the route, how often, and how long it is given are not stated. The main outcome is safety and tolerability, and the study also looks at dose-limiting toxicities, biologically effective doses, pharmacokinetics, and anti-leukemic effects.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa BP1002, un oligodesoxinucleótido antisentido liposomal dirigido a Bcl-2, en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda (LMA) refractaria o en recaída. BP1002 se administra primero solo en dosis crecientes y después en combinación con decitabina; la vía, la frecuencia y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. El resultado principal es la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, y el estudio también analiza las toxicidades limitantes de dosis, las dosis biológicamente efectivas, la farmacocinética y los efectos antileucémicos.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with refractory or relapsed AML that did not respond to available active therapies
For the expansion phase, eligible to receive decitabine
Adequate liver and kidney function, including creatinine clearance of at least 60 mL/min
Agree to use contraception and able to give written informed consent
not_for: Active non-blood cancer, or other cancer treated within the past 12 months
Acute promyelocytic leukemia with PML-RARA, or chronic myeloid leukemia
Anti-cancer therapy within 14 days before the first dose, or other investigational agents
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or uncontrolled heart, seizure, or other conditions that may interfere with study participation
